content: 1. Avoid coadministration of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates with ivosidenib, or replace them with alternative therapies. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor patients for reduced therapeutic effects of these drugs. 2. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior larotrectinib dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3–5 half-lives. 3. Lasmiditan increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 6. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of leniolisib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel (intrauterine) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptives instead. 9. Lopinavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lorlatinib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 11. Lorlatinib decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lovotibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals (ARTs) at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period. ARTs may interfere with lovotibeglogene autotemcel manufacturing. 13. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 14. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of macitentan with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 15. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Nelfinavir increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Increased toxicity risk exists. Avoid coadministration during and for 15 weeks after discontinuing mefloquine. 17. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of midazolam (intranasal) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases midazolam systemic exposure, potentially prolonging sedation. 18. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of adverse reactions, especially during the first week of treatment. 19. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of neratinib with strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of nirogacestat by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of olaparib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose to 150 mg (capsule) or 100 mg (tablet) PO BID. Do not substitute tablets with capsules. 22. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of omaveloxolone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects emerge. 23. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of osimertinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of osimertinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If no alternative exists, monitor the patient closely for adverse effects. 24. Nelfinavir increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Oxycodone dose reduction may be warranted when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of palbociclib with strong CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palbociclib dose to 75 mg/day. 26. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pazopanib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, decrease the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day. 28. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose (refer to drug monograph for dosage modifications). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 29. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose (refer to drug monograph for dosage modifications). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 30. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pimavanserin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Decrease the dose to 17 mg/day if pimavanserin is coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pirtobrutinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg qDay, discontinue pirtobrutinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 32. Nelfinavir increases pomalidomide levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ponatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Decrease the ponatinib starting dose to 30 mg qDay if coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided. 34. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of pralsetinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone (intravaginal gel) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone (micronized) by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of quazepam by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Quinidine increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Nelfinavir increases quinidine levels by decreasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ranolazine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of red yeast rice by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase creatine kinase levels and the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is reportedly identical to lovastatin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 43. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be coadministered with ribociclib, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 44. Rifabutin decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Nelfinavir increases rifabutin levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Rifapentine decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 46. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat by decreasing metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the dose if needed. 48. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. 49. Nelfinavir increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID with a platelet count ≥100 x 10^9/L and concurrent use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Avoid use with platelet counts <100 x 10^9/L. 51. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage (refer to the selumetinib monograph for further information). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 53. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 54. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 55. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 56. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 57. Sotorasib decreases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If use is unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. 58. Nelfinavir and sparsentan increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, interrupt treatment with sparsentan. When resuming sparsentan, consider dose titration. 59. St. John’s Wort decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of stiripentol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 61. Nelfinavir increases the levels of suvorexant by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
